results.name: SEG Solar opens 4 GW Texas facility, announces plan to become the nation’s largest crystalline silicon module maker - pv magazine USA
results.content:
# SEG Solar opens 4 GW Texas facility, announces plan to become the nation’s largest crystalline silicon module maker  
SEG Solar has opened its newest facility, a 4 GW solar module assembly plant in Tomball, Texas. Once the plant is fully operational next year, it will bring SEG’s annual module assembly capacity to 6 GW, joining the company’s original 2 GW facility in nearby Houston.  
As part of the grand opening ceremonies, SEG also announced plans to build an additional 4.6 GW module assembly factory within 18 months. The new facility would be located across the street from the new Tomball plant and bring the company’s total annual capacity to 10.6 GW, making it the largest crystalline silicon solar module assembler in the United States.  
In addition to the new module capacity, the company said it plans to build a solar cell manufacturing plant in the U.S. by 2028.  
The announcement of plans for cell capacity came on an auspicious day — less than 24 hours prior to the grand opening ceremony, the Trump administration unveiled [a plan to implement a price floor and additional tariffs](https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/08/07/us-announces-tariffs-minimum-import-price-on-polysilicon-imports/) levied on all imported solar cells and modules under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.
During the ceremony, emcee (and SEG general counsel) Michael Eden referred to the company’s impending need to make decisions about how to respond to the tariffs as “a tall order” for CEO Jim Wood, but expressed confidence in the CEO’s abilities.  
“We’re all looking to Jim to pull a rabbit out of the hat, and tell us how we’re going to navigate this next challenge for the solar industry,” Eden said.  
The ceremony included numerous speakers in addition to Eden and Wood, including SEG VP of operations Timothy Johnson, senior VP of DEPCOM Power Natasha Cherenkova, Paul Wormser of Intertek CEA, Nico Johnson of Suncast Media and local business leaders.  
The final presentation of the event was given by SEG founder and COO Jun Zhuge, who unveiled the company’s plans for expanding its stateside module assembly and cell manufacturing capacity. Zhuge said the company’s U.S. facilities would reach a production level of 70,000 modules a day when the second Tomball factory added 4.6 GW of new capacity in 2027.  
Zhuge closed his portion of the event by displaying a slide with a timeline that extended to 2029, with a photograph of the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City and a heading that read “IPO?”  
Following Zhuge’s speech, all the speakers gathered on stage to officially open the plant with a ceremonial switch-throwing, and the company welcomed guests on a tour of the facility.  
**Plans for operation and employment**
**Plans for operation and employment**  
During the tour, SEG operations VP Johnson led a group of attendees through the facility, walking step-by-step through the manufacturing lines.  
The plant is made with three front-end lines, consisting of cell-stringing and glass and encapsulant layup machines; eight giant lamination machines; and four output lines.  
He said that when fully operational, the lines would run 7 days per week, 20 hours per day, with time for maintenance and employee breaks.  
SEG plans to start pilot calibration of the facility within the next few weeks, bringing on 100 workers to start the lines up. Those workers are now being trained at the company’s original Houston facility.  
At full capacity, the Tomball facility is expected to be staffed by 500 workers and produce as many as 30,000 solar modules per day.

results.name: SEG Solar opens 4 GW Tomball factory; previously announced third facility would push total to 10.6 GW
results.content:
[SEG Solar opened a new 4-gigawatt solar module assembly plant in Tomball, Texas on August 7](https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/08/10/seg-solar-opens-4-gw-texas-facility-announces-plan-to-become-the-nations-largest-crystalline-silicon-module-maker/), marking one of the largest single-facility additions to American solar module manufacturing capacity in recent years.  
At the grand-opening ceremony, the Houston-based company highlighted a [previously announced third factory](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/seg-solar-announces-third-us-factory-becoming-largest-domestic-solar-manufacturer-at-10-6-gw-capacity-302787073.html) that would push its total planned domestic capacity to 10.6 GW, a figure the company says would make it the largest crystalline silicon solar module assembler in the United States.
## What opened and what it can produce  
The SEG Solar Tomball facility officially opened on August 7, 2026, as a 4 GW solar module assembly plant. Once fully operational next year, it will bring SEG’s annual module assembly capacity to 6 GW, joining the company’s original 2 GW facility in nearby Houston.  
The facility runs three front-end production lines, eight lamination machines and four output lines. At full capacity it is expected to employ 500 workers producing as many as 30,000 modules a day.  
The nearly 500,000-square-foot plant represents more than $200 million in investment and could create up to 800 new jobs.  
Commercial operations were slated to begin in the third quarter of 2026, with pilot calibration starting in the weeks following the grand opening and 100 workers, trained at the Houston plant, running the lines first.
## A third factory announced ahead of the opening ceremony  
SEG Solar announced plans on June 1, 2026 to develop a third U.S. manufacturing facility in Greater Houston, Texas. The new 4.6 GW facility is expected to bring SEG’s planned annual U.S. module manufacturing capacity to 10.6 GW. As part of the grand opening ceremonies, the company reiterated plans to build the additional 4.6 GW module assembly factory within 18 months. The new facility would be located across the street from the Tomball plant and bring the company’s total annual capacity to 10.6 GW, making it the largest crystalline silicon solar module assembler in the United States.  
SEG has signed an agreement with a local construction company to develop the new 4.6 GW facility on a site spanning approximately 1.15 million square feet, including a factory and warehouse. Construction is projected to be completed by March 2027, with commercial production expected to begin in May 2027.  
In addition to the new module capacity, the company said it plans to build a solar cell manufacturing plant in the U.S. by 2028. The third facility will produce heterojunction technology (HJT) modules, which would boost the number of n-type solar panels made in America as TOPCon patent disputes continue to work through the courts.
